correctness.rationale: At θ=π, nonnegativity gives b+c≥a−1, and at 4π/5 all three cosine factors equal r=−(1+√5)/4, giving a+b+c≤√5−1. Thus a≤√5/2. Equality makes both contacts zero and the derivative condition −a+4b−6c=0 solves b=(7√5−12)/20, c=(3√5−8)/20 uniquely. With x=cosθ, independent exact Chebyshev expansion verifies (x+1)(x−r)²R(x). R′(x) has negative leading coefficient and strictly negative discriminant 32(1063−477√5)/25<0, so R decreases on ℝ and R(x)≥R(1)=−1+3√5/5>0 on [−1,1]. Hence global feasibility and uniqueness.
